_meta.author: Mistral Vibe (mistral-vibe)
_meta.purpose: Three changes from the complete ground truth's correction families, under a split-half held-out protocol (md5(filename) first hex char: even = authoring half, 132 records; odd = measurement half, 108): (1) v8's subject-decides clause for representation, refined -- 'statue, sculpture, figurine, or display model' instead of 'model', plus 'a real, functioning robot or machine is photograph' (v8's 'model' over-applied to photographed robots); (2) text_screenshot extended to software interfaces, the first held-out test of the interface family (16 `other` -> text_screenshot corrections; v3's broadening was a measured negative on the personal collection); (3) contains_human yes counts a person visible anywhere -- small, partial, background, or reflection (6 no -> yes corrections).
design_notes: Split-half held-out protocol: with ground truth complete (240/240), no unseen batch remains; the split is deterministic (md5(filename)[0] hex parity) and every correction family has members in both halves (statue 13/9, interface 8/8, background-people 4/3). Authored from the authoring half's corrections only; measured on the measurement half (measure_taxonomy_v9.py) against v7's stored answers.

The subject-decides clause is v8's, refined: v8 measured inside noise (fixes 5 / breaks 3, 3 of 8 run-to-run variance; the clause's 'model' over-applied to photographed robots). v9 sharpens the wording and adds the functioning-robot exception.

The interface broadening is v3's change re-tested held-out on the corpus: v3 regressed on the personal collection (representation 76% -> 69%, photographed covers called text_screenshot). The corpus's 16 interface corrections are the new evidence; the measurement half's 8 are the test.

contains_human.instructions: Does this image contain a human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more humans (people, faces, bodies) in any medium: photographed, drawn, illustrated, rendered, sculpted (a statue or figurine), or sketched in a diagram. A character depicted in a cartoon, card, or illustration is visible and counts. A person visible anywhere in the image counts -- even small, partial, in the background, or in a reflection. A person merely mentioned, named, or described in text within the image does not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no humans: no person, face, or body is visible in any medium (people only mentioned or described in text do not count). A robot or android, however human-like, is not a human for this question

contains_robot.instructions: Does this image contain a robot or mechanical automaton?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more robots: mechanical automatons with a being-like form -- a body, face, or limbs -- whether photographed, illustrated, or rendered. Abstract machinery, engines, or mechanisms without a being-like form do not count; robots merely mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no robots or mechanical automatons with a being-like form (machinery without a body or face, and robots only mentioned in text, do not count)

contains_android.instructions: Does this image contain an android: an artificial being that passes as human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more androids: artificial beings manufactured to pass as human -- a human face, skin, and human proportions, presented as a person. Only what is visible in any medium counts; beings merely described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no androids: no artificial being presented as human-passing. A visibly mechanical robot -- exposed machinery, metal or plastic skin, glowing or camera eyes -- is not an android, even if humanoid in shape (beings only mentioned in text do not count)

primary_subject.instructions: What is the primary humanoid subject of the image?

criteria.human: The main subject the image itself shows, in any medium (photo, illustration, render, sculpture, diagram), is one or more humans; humans only mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.robot: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more robots or mechanical automatons with a being-like form; abstract machinery and robots only mentioned in text do not count
criteria.android: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more androids: artificial beings with a human-passing appearance (human face, skin, and proportions), not visibly mechanical robots
criteria.multiple: The image itself prominently shows more than one distinct kind of humanoid (e.g., a human together with a robot)
criteria.none: The image shows no humanoid subject of any kind, in any medium: no human, robot, or android is visible, whether photographed, drawn, rendered, or sculpted. Images that are only text, objects, or scenes without humanoids are 'none' -- a humanoid described in text is not depicted

criteria.photograph: A photograph of a real scene: actual people, objects, or places captured by a camera -- but the image being a photograph does not decide this facet: if the subject is a statue, sculpture, figurine, or display model, it is statue_or_render; if the subject is a drawing, painting, or poster, it is illustration. A photograph of a real, functioning robot, machine, or vehicle is photograph
criteria.illustration: A drawing, cartoon, comic, painting, or digital illustration -- including one photographed or scanned; but if the subject is a statue, sculpture, figurine, or display model, it is statue_or_render
criteria.statue_or_render: A statue, figurine, sculpture, scale model, display model, or 3D render of a subject
criteria.text_screenshot: A screenshot or scan of text or a software interface: the image shows words, code, or an application interface (window, website, terminal), not a photographed scene
criteria.other: None of the above: a diagram, chart, map, or abstract image
